editorial:
Imagine you are out in the middle of nowhere on a dusty dig site with a partner. You think you are just finding old bones, but you actually stumble upon a vampire burial ground. That is exactly where you start in this 1973 flick. The vibe is very old-school and spooky, focusing on two archaeologists who realize they have woken up something terrible. Once the vampires start stirring, the danger spreads to a nearby village, and you get to watch the chaos unfold as the locals try to survive the night.

What really works here is the slow build-up of dread and the campy 70s style. The acting is a bit stiff, but that just adds to the charm of this kind of horror. If you love movies where people make bad decisions for the sake of science, you will have a blast. Since this is a rare find, you should definitely try renting it on Apple TV or streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see those vintage colors pop. If you are a real movie buff, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the archaeologists realize that the only way to stop the massacre is to destroy the heart of the vampire queen. After a big fight with the undead horde, they manage to trap Hannah and kill her for good. Once the queen dies, the other vampires lose their power and turn back to dust. The village is saved, and the survivors are left to pick up the pieces of their broken town.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school vampire movies and retro horror.
